title: Director, Regional Sales
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As the Director of Regional Sales for Japan, you'll own the strategy and execution to grow GitLab's presence across Japan. You'll build and manage an Account Executive team, establish clear, data-informed sales processes, and stay close to the field by engaging directly with key accounts. Reporting to our Country Manager, Japan, you'll work across account management, customer success, marketing, product, engineering, and operations to deliver a consistent, high-quality experience for GitLab customers and expand our footprint. In this role, you'll help shape GitLab's go-to-market motion in Japan, support new logo acquisition and expansion, and influence how we bring our Governed Software Factory and DevSecOps value proposition to a broad range of customers while supporting regional business priorities.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Oversee the growth of GitLab's business in Japan by building the regional sales plan, maintaining pipeline visibility, and guiding day-to-day execution in support of regional business plans.</li> <li>Manage, coach, and develop a team of Account Executives, joining customer meetings and modeling consistent, field-focused sales practices.</li> <li>Support new logo acquisition across a broad base of Enterprise businesses in Japan, while shaping and executing a long-term strategy for larger, more complex, multi-stakeholder accounts, including guiding deal strategy and contract negotiations for high-value opportunities.</li> <li>Build GitLab's reputation in the Japan market by partnering with marketing, business development, and local networks to generate qualified pipelines and deepen market awareness.</li> <li>Establish clear operating rhythms, sales processes, and methodologies (such as MEDDPICC or similar) that create structure and repeatability while supporting agility.</li> <li>Work with regional sales managers and cross-functional partners in account management, customer success, marketing, product, engineering, and operations to align coverage, exchange practices, and ensure consistent execution.</li> <li>Develop and maintain executive-level relationships with key accounts, positioning GitLab as a strategic partner and uncovering expansion and renewal opportunities.</li> <li>Review pipeline, forecast, and performance data to identify gaps and opportunities, adjust regional plans to focus on priority activities, and represent the Japan business internally with clear insights on market trends and customer needs.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building and managing sales teams in a regional or multi-country context, with a focus on coaching, field engagement, and talent development.</li> <li>Ability to design and execute a regional go-to-market plan, including pipeline generation, territory coverage, and structured deal execution.</li> <li>Ability to coach teams through a clear sales process, assist with complex deal strategy, and maintain consistency in regional execution.</li> <li>Familiarity with B2B software sales / technology sales and AI accelerated workflows and platforms.</li> <li>Skills in creating structure and clarity, setting expectations, and using organized, data-informed sales processes, including the use of MEDDPICC or similar methodologies.</li> <li>Demonstrated strength in consultative, value-based selling and in developing established relationships with senior customer stakeholders to assist with new business and expansion.</li> <li>Comfort working in a dynamic, all-remote environment, using sound judgment, initiative, and Salesforce.com or similar CRM and marketing tools to stay organized and effective.</li> <li>Ability to work effectively across account management, customer success, marketing, product, engineering, and operations to align execution and enable customer growth.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We are the regional sales team for Japan, and our focus is on growing the business by building strong customer relationships, developing the field organisation, and partnering across GitLab to deliver a consistent experience for our customers.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> advocates.</li> <li>Advise customers on modern software development, continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), security, and cloud practices to improve their return on investment.</li> <li>Share customer feedback, use cases, and competitive insights with Product Management, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing while continuing to build expertise and reusable guidance in GitLab, DevSecOps, AI, and cloud technologies.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience guiding Commercial and Enterprise customers through solution design and evaluation in technical presales, consulting, or a similar role.</li> <li>Experience working with India's GCCs, Digital Native organizations, and startups is highly valued.</li> <li>Knowledge of the end-to-end software development lifecycle, including modern DevSecOps practices and CI/CD workflows.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with GitLab or comparable source control, CI/CD, and collaboration platforms, operations options.</li> <li>Ability to lead proofs of concept or value, contribute to tenders or audits, and design and run workshops or value stream assessments.</li> <li>Clear technical communication and presentation skills, with the ability to adapt your message for practitioners and senior business and technical decision-makers.</li> <li>Skill in building trusted relationships, title: Revenue Cycle Manager
description: About Us We are fixing US healthcare by building an AI-native physical care platform, starting with home health. Home health is a $140B industry with less than $10B in EBITDA â 40% of revenue is spent on pure administrative waste. We automate this work with AI, creating a fundamentally different cost structure compared to incumbents. This lets us rapidly take market share by serving the 30% of patients who go untreated today. By reshaping the cost structure of this industry, we unlock its growth. We've built one of the best AI teams in the world (from Character AI, Scale, Palantir, Citadel, Jane Street) and paired them with a team of healthcare veterans to build a new type of healthcare company: one that delivers care at the speed of an AI company. Our physical care platform already operates with 30pp higher gross margins than traditional home health providers. With our AI advantage, we pay nurses more, remove their admin burden, and unlock the scale economics that have been missing from this fragmented industry. If we served this entire $140B market, instead of $10B in EBITDA, we'd drive $60B. We're starting with home health, then expanding to all delivered care. Our mission is "any care, any where" . Fundamentally, our incentives are aligned with America. Every dollar in revenue we make is two dollars taken out of the healthcare system. If we succeed, so does US healthcare. Role overview Weâre seeking a hands-on Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) Manager to lead and support a team of specialists in a home health environment. This manager will stay close to daily operations, monitor team performance, and respond quickly to questions and emerging issues to help the team meet its goals. The role focuses on accounts receivable (AR), helping the team move outstanding claims from follow-up to verified resolution. What Youâll Do Manage and support RCM specialists working across home health revenue cycle workflows. Track attendance and monitor individual and team performance against established KPIs and daily quotas. Review workflow boards throughout the day to spot backlogs, red flags, and specialists at risk of missing their end-of-day quotas. Respond promptly to specialist questions while balancing real-time workflow monitoring and other team needs. Identify process gaps and work with the team to resolve issues affecting daily performance. Apply your home health and Homecare Homebase (HCHB) knowledge to help specialists navigate workflows and resolve operational questions. Accounts receivable and collections Guide specialists and team leads in prioritizing assigned commercial, Medicare, and Medicare Advantage receivables, including aged balances, payer responses, rejections, denials, and upcoming filing or appeal deadlines. Oversee claim follow-up through resolution: verify claim status and payment, investigate collection barriers and underpayments, and guide appropriate corrections, reprocessing, reconsiderations, or appeals under payer-specific requirements. Review and respond to escalations when a specialist cannot determine the next action; surface recurring payer, workflow, or system issues to leadership and coordinate their resolution. Ensure claim activity, supporting evidence, next actions, and follow-up dates are documented accurately in the applicable AR workflow and HCHB. Partner with billing, payment posting, prior authorization, clinical, and other teams to resolve discrepancies, obtain documentation, and follow paid-but-not-posted claims through resolution. Review proposed write-offs for documented collection efforts and supporting evidence, and route them through the required approval and posting process. Quality and team development Review claim work for accurate denial interpretation, appropriate action, complete documentation, timely follow-up, and correct escalation; use findings to coach specialists and strengthen performance. Support onboarding, payer and system cross-training, and regular knowledge sharing. Identify patterns behind collection challenges and update SOPs or workflows to prevent repeat issues. Share frontline feedback on AR dashboards and automation with relevant teams to improve prioritization, visibility, and specialist workflows. Basic Qualifications Strong experience in home health revenue cycle operations. Familiarity with Homecare Homebase (HCHB). Experience managing RCM specialists, including tracking attendance and performance KPIs. Experience monitoring workflows throughout the day and identifying risks to daily productivity targets. Experience identifying collection challenges and implementing processes to resolve. Working knowledge of AR follow-up, denial investigation, appeals or reprocessing, and payer-specific filing requirements. Experience reviewing claim documentation and quality, escalating unresolved issues, and coordinating with billing or posting teams. Ability to respond promptly to team questions while managing multiple priorities. Ability to identify workflow or process gaps and help the team address them. Preferred Qualifications Experience managing distributed or offshore revenue cycle teams. Familiarity with commercial fee-for-service and Medicare or Medicare Advantage home health claims, including episodic/PDGM workflows. Experience with AR dashboards, clearinghouses, and payer portals such as Waystar and Availity. Experience using denial trends, quality reviews, or operational data to improve collections workflows and team training. What We Offer Competitive salary Comprehensive health insurance, dental, and commuter benefits 401(k) retirement plan with employer contribution Opportunity for growth in a fast-growing company Collaborative team valuing innovation and problem-solving Please mention the word **MAJESTY** and tag RNTIuMTY1LjU5LjUy when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RNTIuMTY1LjU5LjUy). title: Senior Product Manager
description: About us At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. The role Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer. You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients. You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job. Key responsibilities Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list. Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them. Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs. Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses. Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path. Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended. Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client. Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse. Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards. Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need. Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework. Your background You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through: A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there. Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with. Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working. A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role. A decision you changed because the data told you to. Fluent in qual and quant. Experience with AI agents or AI-assisted products is a plus. You'll Thrive Here If Youâ¦ Move Fast. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, iterating quickly, and fixing things before they become fires; Stay Human. You care deeply about users and teammates, and design with empathy for real workflows; Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs. You spot problems early and take initiative to fix them. Keep It Simple. You fight unnecessary complexity, design reusable patterns, and make hard things feel intuitive. Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability. KPIs & Success Measures We will measure success through outcomes and quality, not just output: Builder share (lead): percentage of monthly active users who build or edit a workflow. Target [TBD]%. Workflow adoption (lead): percentage of monthly active users who run a workflow. Target [TBD]%. Workflow run growth: month-on-month percentage growth in workflow runs. Target [TBD]%. First workflow conversion: percentage of new users who complete a successful run within their first [TBD] days. Share of generations through workflows: percentage of all generations produced by workflow runs. Agent and human collaboration: percentage of workflow runs built or started by Scribble. Connector adoption: percentage of active workspaces that use at least one third-party connection in a workflow each month. Target [TBD]%. Integration usage: percentage of workflow runs that start from, or deliver to, a third-party connection. Target [TBD]%. Reliability (hygiene bar): percentage of runs that complete without manual intervention, held at or above [TBD]%. Learning velocity (supporting): percentage of launches reviewed after release against their stated hypothesis. Target 100%. Benefits 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme Health insurance / private medical cover Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development Remote - work from anywhere in your home country Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for our UK employees Flexible working hours Deep Dive About Pencil Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI. We're called Pencil because we believe AI will be a tool for creative people, not a replacement - it may even be as fundamental a tool in the future as the pencil was in the past. Pencil was founded in 2018 with a team from Google, Facebook and Uber with backing from Sequoia and Entrepreneur First. We were acquired by The Brandtech Group in 2023 to pursue a shared vision of bringing GenAI to the Fortune 500. https://www.trypencil.com About The Brandtech Group The Brandtech Group's mission is to be the best company in the world at helping leading global brands drive growth by connecting content, data and media using technology. It was founded in June 2015 (as You & Mr Jones) by former Havas Global CEO David Jones, with a simple mission to help brands do their marketing better, faster and cheaper using technology. It was renamed The Brandtech Group in January 2022. Today it generates more than $1BN in revenue and is the largest global digital content partner for many of the world's biggest brands and companies, often using its unique in-housing model. It works with eight of the world's top 10 global advertisers and 49 of the world's top 100. Clients include Banco ItaÃº, Danone, Google, Intuit, LVMH, Microsoft, Morgan-Stanley, Netflix, Reckitt, Renault-Nissan, PayPal, TikTok, Uber and Unilever. In addition, the Group invests in cutting-edge technology companies relevant to and with potential in marketing and has been investing in the AI, AR and the metaverse space since 2015. The Group was the first external investor in Niantic (creators of PokÃ©mon Go), alongside investments in AI Foundation (AI digital twins, personalized AI, and deep-fake detection 2018), Automat (AI chatbots, 2016), Elsy (AI media planning, 2016), Jivox (dynamic automated content, 2016), Crossing Minds (deep learning AI recommendation system, 2017), CreativeX (AI-driven content optimization, 2022), Zappar (AR, 2017), Provenance (blockchain, 2022) and GGP (the world's largest gaming fund). The Group is one of the most prominent marketing industry voices on the prediction and movement to AI-driven marketing, including Generative AI. It was named one of the World's Most Innovative Companies 2021 by Fast Company, and by CB Insights as one of the World's Most Valuable Private Unicorns. https://www.thebrandtechgroup.com Please mention the word **NICELY** and tag RNTIuMTY1LjU5LjUy when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RNTIuMTY1LjU5LjUy). description: Unió Digital is an Arizona-based managed service provider (MSP) delivering Managed IT Services, Low Voltage Cabling, Access Control, Video Surveillance, and Intrusion Services. Connect invitations, onboarding, event follow-up, ongoing engagement, and reporting so SELF and other programs scale without losing personalization.</li> <li>Build SELF's annual programming and marketing calendar. Coordinate experiences with GitLab's broader campaigns, launches, field activities, and marketing priorities.</li> <li>Put AI to work in community marketing. Experiment with ways to automate workflows, understand member feedback, personalize content, and make better decisions. Apply human judgment, review outputs for quality, and handle member data responsibly.</li> <li>Partner with Sales and Customer Success to identify priority accounts and top customer champions. Build relevant paths for them to join and contribute to community programs as members, speakers, and peer leaders, with coordinated outreach and follow-up.</li> <li>Collaborate with internal executive teams and crossfunctional partners, as well as external community partners to seed growth and integrate across existing plans. </li> <li>Track, measure and iterate on membership growth, event participation and quality, activation, retention, satisfaction, priority-account engagement, and advocacy. </li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building or scaling communities, membership programs, or peer networks.</li> <li>Ability to turn strategy into a clear growth plan, annual programming and marketing calendar, and coordinated member journey.</li> <li>An understanding of how community, customer engagement, advocacy, and account growth reinforce one another.</li> <li>Experience partnering closely with sales teams to identify priority accounts and customer champions and engage them in relevant programs.</li> <li>Demonstrated experience planning and delivering both virtual and in-person events, including community events. Ability to connect audience selection, programming, speaker engagement, and follow-up to member value and measurable outcomes.</li> <li>Familiarity with lifecycle marketing, marketing automation, CRM systems, web analytics, or campaign measurement.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional collaboration and writing skills, with the ability to communicate a program's value to different audiences.</li> <li>Ability to use member research, event feedback, engagement data, and marketing results to make decisions and improve programs.</li> <li>Sound judgment and the ability to balance ownership of SELF with marketing support for other community programs, working with operational partners on delivery.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the Team </strong></p> <p>The Growth Community Programs team supports GitLab’s growth flywheel, seeding tomorrow’s customers and activating today’s. title: GTM, Strategic Planning
description: Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search — all deeply integrated and designed for growth. We're building the best developer platform to power the next generation of software companies, and our go-to-market team is scaling fast to match. We're looking for a lead in Go-To-Market Strategic Planning, to shape how Supabase's GTM engine runs. This is a high-leverage, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of strategy, data, and execution. You'll work directly with Success, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Partnerships and Product to build the systems, processes, and insights that help our go-to-market teams move faster and smarter. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the end-to-end GTM Strategic Planning, covering territory design, segmentation design, target planning and GTM capacity planning. - Build and maintain a single source of truth for planning data across HubSpot, BigQuery and Hex. - Translate company priorities into field actions through designing the planning strategy and seeing it through to execution. - Partner with Sales Leadership to design and iterate on coverage models, segmentation, and team structures that reflect how developers actually buy. - Define and track the metrics that matter, and surface insights that drive action, not just reporting. - Lead the Strategic Planning roadmap: guide and lead in tooling investments and evaluate new systems and processes against real business needs. - Work cross-functionally with talent acquisition, ensuring GTM and territory models stay aligned. - Collaborate with GTM Engineering on automations and data pipelines so that your strategy translates into working systems, not just slide decks. WE'LL EXPECT YOU TO - Operate with high ownership. You set your own agenda, escalate when needed, and don't wait to be asked. - Work asynchronously and document clearly. We're a globally distributed team and writing is how we think. - Bridge strategy and execution. From drafting segmentation approaches in Google Docs to using SQL to monitor its effectiveness. - Build for scale without over-engineering. Simple systems that work beat perfect systems that don't ship. - Stay close to the customer. Developers are our buyers, and understanding how they discover, adopt, and expand is core to everything you'll do. YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU - Have 6+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Strategy Consulting, GTM Strategy, or Sales Operations at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company. - Are fluent in the GTM stack: HubSpot, BigQuery, and Hightouch. - Can write SQL comfortably and aren't afraid to get into the data yourself before asking an analyst. - Have experience designing or overhauling sales processes, forecasting cadences, or territory models in a high-growth environment. - Understand product-led growth motions: PLS, usage-based triggers, and how PLG data flows into commercial pipelines. - Thrive with autonomy and are energized by building things that didn't exist before you joined. - Communicate with clarity across Finance, Sales, Success, Partnerships, Engineering, and Marketing without losing nuance. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

You'll join a Rust-first team that values clear ownership, thoughtful system design, and rigorous thinking about data and reliability.</p> <p>The Knowledge Graph service is a Rust backend that builds a property graph from GitLab’s software development lifecycle (SDLC) and code data. It uses ClickHouse, NATS JetStream, and the Data Insights Platform. It exposes secure graph queries and MCP tools used by AI agents and product features. In this role, you’ll deliver features and improvements in well-scoped areas, learn the broader architecture, and contribute to reliability, observability, and operational readiness.</p> <p>In your first year, you’ll take clear ownership of specific components or features (for example, parts of the SDLC indexing pipeline or query paths). You’ll help reduce single points of failure with better tests and runbooks, and you’ll help the team ship analytical services that are easier to maintain and evolve over time.</p> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">What you’ll do</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1">Implement and iterate on backend features in the Rust-based Knowledge Graph service, including changes to the query engine, SDLC and code indexing flows, and API endpoints (including MCP endpoints) under guidance from senior and staff engineers.</li> <li value="2">Maintain integrations between Knowledge Graph and the rest of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform.</li> <li value="3">Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads.</li> <li value="4">Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience.</li> <li value="5">Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team.</li> <li value="6">Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly (for example, using Knowledge Graph-backed agents and internal Duo tooling), and share what workflows and evaluation methods.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Lead backend features from early product discussions through technical design, implementation, rollout, and post-launch learning.</li> <li>Build the flows, application programming interfaces, and data models behind agent-generated work items, implementation plans, durable specifications, and mergeable clearly in GitLab's asynchronous, all-remote environment.</li> <li>Mentor other engineers and contribute to technical direction across the Plan group and related artificial intelligence initiatives.</li> <li>Work in short iterations, share progress through demos, and use results and user feedback to guide what comes next.</li> <li><span data-sheets-root="1">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</span></li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Strong Ruby on Rails experience in a large production codebase and production experience with Python.</li> <li>Experience driving substantial projects with several engineers over multiple months, with clear user or business outcomes.</li> <li>A product mindset and experience owning features end to end, including shaping scope, making trade-offs, engaging with users, and learning from adoption after launch.</li> <li>A full stack background with a current focus on backend engineering, plus the ability to read modern frontend code and design effective APIs.</li> <li>Strong application programming interface design and structured query language fundamentals.</li> <li>Experience exploring artificial intelligence-assisted development.</li> <li>The ability to work independently, collaborate across functions and regions, and support others through technical leadership and mentoring. Experience with GraphQL, PostgreSQL performance at scale, or building and evaluating large language model or agent systems is helpful but not required.</li> </ul> <p>We welcome candidates with different backgrounds and transferable experience. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply.</p> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We are a team of four engineers, with two backend and two frontend engineers across Canada and Europe. You'll work in an all-remote, async-first environment with weekly sync calls, retrospectives, demos, and short iterations. This is early-stage work with broad ownership, space for creativity, and a fast pace. title: Business Development Representative
location: Remote, Ireland; Remote, Spain; Remote, United Kingdom
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>This is a future opportunity that may not be immediately available, but we're proactively building our pipeline of exceptional talent. At GitLab, we believe in connecting with outstanding professionals before we have an urgent need, allowing us to move quickly when the right moment arises. If you are excited about co-creating the future as we're building the most comprehensive AI-powered DevSecOps platform, we want to hear from you. We'll keep your information on file and reach out when a position becomes available that matches your skills and interests.</strong></p> <h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>This position is 100% remote and will be based in the UK, Ireland, and Spain.<br><br>GitLab is looking for an enthusiastic and strategic Business Development Representative (BDR) to join our growing Sales team. As a BDR at GitLab, you get the opportunity to lead the initial outreach to targeted accounts working in conjunction with the Field and Digital Marketing teams as well as the Sales and Customer Success teams. In this role you'll leverage creative marketing and sales tactics to prospect and engage with multiple buyer personas and roles to introduce GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You'll be responsible for generating qualified meetings and pipeline for GitLab's Sales organization.</p> <p>Our BDRs come from a diverse background. Many have worked in closing roles previously or managed teams.</p> <p>We have an extensive onboarding and training program at GitLab and you'll be provided with necessary DevOps and GitLab knowledge to fulfill your role.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Execute outbound prospecting initiatives to generate qualified meetings and pipeline in your assigned territory.</li> <li>Generate New Logo opportunities and Growth opportunities on existing customer accounts.</li> <li>Conduct high-level discovery conversations with target accounts to understand business needs, qualify opportunities, and create Sales Accepted Opportunities (SAOs).</li> <li>Meet or exceed monthly and quarterly BDR-sourced Sales Accepted Opportunity (SAO) targets (e.g., Stage 1 and Stage 3 opportunities) by consistently converting qualified prospects into opportunities.</li> <li>Research and prioritize target accounts using business and industry knowledge to identify key players, uncover compelling events, and develop tailored outreach strategies.</li> <li>Execute a multi-touch outreach cadence (call, email, social, etc.) to all prospects in your assigned territory using Outreach to maximize engagement and conversion rates.</li> <li>Manage, track, and accurately report all prospecting activities and pipeline in Salesforce to provide clear visibility into performance and forecast.</li> <li>Collaborate with Field, Corporate, and Digital Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success teams to build targeted account lists, campaigns, and call strategies. Attend regional marketing events to engage participants, generate leads, and drive qualified Sales Accepted Opportunities (SAOs).</li> <li>Document and continuously improve Business Development Representative processes in the GitLab handbook in partnership with your Business Development Manager. Mentor new BDR hires to help them ramp quickly and navigate key accounts.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Positive and energetic phone skills, excellent listening skills, strong writing skills.</li> <li>Ability to prioritize tasks, manage a high volume of outreach, and consistently follow through on prospecting activities.</li> <li>Proven experience taking initiative, persisting through setbacks, and independently driving projects or activities through to successful outcomes.</li> <li>Alignment with our values and working in accordance with those values.</li> <li>Knowledge of business process, roles, and organizational structure.</li> <li>Proficiency in using Salesforce, Sales Navigator, and Outreach or similar prospecting and sequencing tools.</li> <li>Proficiency in English, our company language, is required for effective communication.</li> <li>Previous tech industry experience or experience in sales development, marketing, or sales is a plus.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>As part of GitLab's growing Sales team, you will work closely with the Field and Digital Marketing teams, as well as the Sales and Customer Success teams. serving Commercialet customers.</li> <li>Ability to quickly learn and sell a complex SaaS or DevSecOps platform to commercial and Commercialet accounts, including identifying and breaking into new customers.</li> <li>Excellence in operational rigor for deal management in Salesforce and Clari (or similar CRM and forecasting tools), with the ability to create reliable forecasts and manage your territory using both insight and data.</li> <li>Skill in managing and closing larger, more complex deals in the Commercial segment using proven multi-threading, negotiation, and executive coverage strategies.</li> <li>Self-starter who is a manager of one when it comes to territory account planning, quarterly and annual KPI execution, and driving new business acquisition and expansion through customer organization, lead clear and compelling customer conversations, and remain calm and solutions-focused under pressure.</li> <li>Experience driving adoption and consumption with customers whilst leading your account team.</li> <li>Outbounding: Not afraid to email, call, prospect into prospective accounts whilst building value narratives that land.</li> <li>Adaptability, flexibility, This role reports to the Senior Director of our Solutions Architecture Center of Excellence, with day-to-day partnership from the current team lead. You'll build and improve the tools, applications, and infrastructure that support field team demos, workshops, trials, and internal test environments across the field. </p> <p>What makes this role unique is its mix of software engineering, infrastructure, and customer-facing collaboration. You'll work like an engineer for much of the role, while also partnering with Solutions Architects, Account Executives, Customer Success, and others to make sure what we build is practical, usable, and aligned to how the field sells.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Build and maintain tools, applications, and workflows that support demos, workshops, trials, and internal test hands-on customer experiences across<a href="https://gitlab.com"> GitLab.com</a>, demo instances, and internal environments.</li> <li>Collaborate with Solutions Architects, Account Executives, Customer Success, Marketing, Revenue Operations, UX, and Engineering to understand needs and deliver practical technical solutions.</li> <li>Learn and document go-to-market workflows (e.g., how teams run demos/workshops/trials) and automate the steps that waste time.</li> <li>Create technical workshop assets and enablement content that support pre-sales and technical selling for individual contributors.</li> <li>Advise on sales opportunities when specialized technical demo support or custom solutions are needed.</li> <li>Improve the presenter experience by reducing manual setup work and making demo workflows easier to use and repeat.</li> <li>Support internal teams that rely on demo or test infrastructure, helping keep those environments available and useful.</li> <li>Troubleshoot urgent demo/workshop environment issues under pressure and communicate status clearly to stakeholders.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building software, documentation.</li> <li>Ability to work across application development and infrastructure, with comfort navigating provisioning, automation, and service workflows.</li> <li>Familiarity with monitoring/observability tools to shorten investigation time when something breaks.</li> <li>Comfort communicating and collaborating with technical and non-technical stakeholders across Sales, correctness, with awareness that the end user may be a seller or Solutions Architect.</li> <li>Ability to operate independently in a remote, asynchronous environment, with willingness to travel periodically for team offsites and occasional in-person planning/whiteboarding sessions.</li> <li>Exposure to technical demos, workshops, trials, or enablement assets, and/or interest in learning the pre-sales context; transferable experience from software engineering, site reliability engineering, systems engineering, solutions architecture, or similar technical paths.   #LI-CM1</li> </ul> You set direction across the data organization, stay close enough to the work to guide technical decisions credibly, and partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, IT, and business leaders.<br>You the AI data access strategy: when to use BI, Claude, MCP servers, or Slack agents, with the governance and security to keep access trusted and reliable</li> <li>Own the enterprise BI and self-service tools strategy (e.g., Tableau, Omni), including evaluation, adoption, and cost</li> <li>Build self-service capabilities, such as Claude skills, documentation, and guided workflows, that help people find and use data on their own</li> <li>Build and own company-wide data applications, from Claude-built single-page apps to apps inside BI tools, that combine Snowflake data, API calls, AI-powered deep dives, and write-back to Postgres or Snowflake</li> <li>Set engineering standards for data apps (security, authentication, testing, deployment, and monitoring) so they're reliable at company scale</li> <li>Set a long-range roadmap tied to company strategy, and a lightweight operating model that balances urgent stakeholder needs with investment in reusable data products and tech-debt reduction</li> <li>Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of 8: build career paths, develop leaders, distribute ownership, and recognize great work</li> <li>Act as customer zero for GitLab and GitLab Duo in data workflows, sharing feedback with Product and Engineering</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>12+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI, including 5+ years leading teams and 2+ years managing managers or senior leads</li> <li>Deep expertise in data modeling and semantic layers (e.g., dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views, LookML, Cube), and expert dbt, including testing and CI/CD across a multi-team project</li> <li>Hands-on experience building LLM-powered data access (text-to-SQL, agents, MCP servers), including evals and telemetry for answer quality, and advanced use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code</li> <li>Expert SQL and strong Snowflake experience; working knowledge of Python</li> <li>Strong data governance experience: data quality, lineage, certified datasets, and access controls (RBAC, row access and masking policies)</li> <li>Track record of leading cross-functional data initiatives from strategy through adoption and measurable business impact, including enterprise BI and self-service at scale</li> <li>Systems thinker who sees how models, pipelines, and architecture decisions connect, and designs for second-order effects</li> <li>Exceptional communicator who writes clear technical specs, sets a clear vision, makes trade-offs visible, and influences executives and peers across the company</li> <li>Pragmatic in ambiguity: makes sound decisions on emerging technology and ships the right next version rather than waiting for the ideal end state</li> <li>Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Nice to Have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience with LLM routing or gateway tools and managing model costs</li> <li>Experience with Tableau, Omni, or a BI platform migration</li> <li>Experience with web app development (e.g., React, TypeScript) and Postgres</li> <li>Experience owning finance or revenue-critical data (e.g., ARR, consumption) where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>Analytics Engineering makes GitLab's data trusted, easy to find, and ready for anyone to use, whether they ask a dashboard, Claude, or a Slack agent. We own the curated data models, the semantic layer, the self-service tools, and the data applications that let teams answer their own questions.</p> <p>AI is changing how people get to data. Questions that once went through an analyst now go straight to AI tools, so the answers are only as good as the data models and business definitions behind them. Our job is to make those answers correct, consistent, and measurable.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. You'll be the strategic finance partner to our Chief Technology Officer (CTO) and their leadership team, owning R&D planning, forecasting, and investment decisions.</p> <p>R&D builds our AI-powered development, security, and operations (DevSecOps) platform, which more than 100,000 organizations use. You'll connect investment in headcount, infrastructure, AI and cloud usage, and tooling to product outcomes, with clear measurement and reliable forecasts.</p> <p>You'll sit at the CTO's staff table, shape GitLab's long-range plan, and help leadership decide where to invest next, making R&D spend predictable.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Serve as the finance advisor to the CTO and R&D leadership. Hold partners accountable for execution against plan and connect R&D priorities to company financial targets.</li> <li>Lead annual planning, and rolling forecasts for R&D. Own the operating plan across headcount, compensation, contractors, hosting and cloud, AI and large language model (LLM) costs, software, and tooling.</li> <li>Build frameworks that connect R&D investment to product roadmap outcomes. Evaluate business cases for new initiatives, AI capabilities, build-versus-buy decisions, and vendor commitments, and present risks and opportunities to leadership.</li> <li>Define and track R&D efficiency metrics, including R&D spend as a percentage of revenue, cost per engineer, hosting cost per user, and AI inference cost per feature. Identify large-scale savings and reallocation opportunities and see them through to completion.</li> <li>Partner with People and R&D leaders on hiring plans, location strategy, and organizational design. Keep headcount forecasts accurate and reconciled to actuals.</li> <li>Lead the AI transformation of R&D finance. Rethink planning, forecasting, and reporting workflows, and use AI tools to make them faster, more accurate, and more insightful.</li> <li>Redesign FP&A processes, policies, and planning and reporting systems for efficiency and effectiveness, with AI in the center. Work with Accounting on capitalized software, accruals, and allocations, and with Procurement on process improvements.</li> <li>Lead and develop your R&D finance team:: hire and coach team members, set goals and priorities, and give expert feedback. Put GitLab's values into practice through handbook-first, asynchronous collaboration across time zones.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Extensive finance experience, including serving as the lead finance partner to an R&D, Engineering, or Product organization plus experience leading a team of analysts</li> <li>A strong understanding of financial statements, accounting principles, and R&D cost drivers, including engineering headcount, cloud hosting, AI and LLM usage, software licenses, and capitalized software development.</li> <li>Experience leading process redesign and change in a finance team, including hands-on use of AI tools to improve how work gets done.</li> <li>Expertise in influencing senior technical stakeholders and translating complex analysis into clear recommendations for executives.</li> <li>Advanced financial modeling skills that follow industry best practices, expertise in Google Sheets, and hands-on experience with financial and data visualization tools. We don't use Excel for modeling.</li> <li>A bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.</li> <li>Comfort working remotely and asynchronously, and the ability to use GitLab.</li> <li>Preferred experience includes enterprise software-as-a-service (SaaS) finance; direct CTO partnership; NetSuite, Sisense, Adaptive Planning, or SQL; or a Master of Business Administration (MBA), Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), or Certified Public Accountant (CPA) qualification.</li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. You will guide long-range platform decisions while partnering with Infrastructure, Product, Distribution, Support, Security, and FinOps. <li>Experience leading managers of managers, including coaching newer managers.</li> <li>Experience working hands-on with PostgreSQL at scale, including capacity planning, upgrades, replication, performance, and large production clusters.</li> <li>Experience using data to make strategic technical decisions and connect database platform investments and tradeoffs with product outcomes.</li> <li>Experience supporting software that customers run themselves, or working through the self-managed upgrade challenge.</li> <li>Experience leading backend engineering teams that own production infrastructure, applying site reliability engineering practices including service level objectives, on-call operations, incident management, cost management, and automation.</li> <li>Experience communicating clearly in writing in an asynchronous, handbook-first company.</li> <li>Experience leading globally distributed remote teams.</li> <li>Experience with Redis, ClickHouse, OpenSearch, object storage, Google Cloud Platform, Kubernetes, Terraform, Chef, managed database services, FinOps, AI-assisted engineering workflows, or platform and infrastructure organizations is a plus.</li> Uphold enterprise-grade SLAs across every tenant.</li> <li>Deliver GitLab Dedicated for Government: AWS GovCloud infrastructure, FedRAMP operations and audit readiness, air-gapped isolation, and public sector feature delivery.</li> <li>Make enterprise migrations to Dedicated predictable, repeatable, and low-disruption through self-service tooling and guided workflows.</li> <li>Hire, coach, and scale engineering managers across distributed teams, and bring practical AI-enabled workflows into how the organization works.</li> <li>Partner with Product, Security, and Customer Support to keep customer commitments, architecture, and investments aligned.</li> <li><span data-sheets-root="1">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</span></li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>You have led engineering organizations that run enterprise single or multi tenant SaaS infrastructure and cloud platforms at scale.</li> architectures, Infrastructure as Code, and modular services that deploy and scale independently across cloud environments.</li> <li>You have delivered and operated enterprise offerings under strict compliance regimes such as FedRAMP and AWS GovCloud.</li> <li>You have led organizational changes, including adopting AI enabled workflows that raise engineering system efficiencies.</li> <li>You translate financial targets into engineering investments, headcount plans, and execution roadmaps.</li> <li>You lead with ownership, speed with quality, and a focus on customer outcomes.</li> </ul> You'll lead senior and principal product managers and be accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue across build, package, deploy, and monitor. Today, these are separate stages with a human making the call at each handoff. As agents take on more coding, pipeline, and deployment work, you'll set the three-year vision for how much of that judgment the system can make safely and how quickly a production signal can turn into a fix without waiting for a human to notice it first. You'll define how customers move from today's manual checkpoints toward agent-driven software delivery at a pace that fits their risk tolerance. leaders, and give customers a credible path for managing software delivery at scale.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the strategy, three-year vision, and business outcomes for GitLab's Agentic Software Delivery section, with a clear point of view on how artificial intelligence is changing software delivery.</li> <li value="2">Lead and develop senior and principal product develop the business cases that support them.</li> <li value="6">Partner with Engineering leadership on platform investment, architectural direction, and trade-offs across the section, while connecting build, package, deploy, and monitor into one coherent customer experience.</li> <li value="7">Drive pricing, packaging, go-to-market strategy, migration, and adoption with Product Marketing, Sales, Pricing, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="8">Represent the section with GitLab's senior leadership, key enterprise customers, partners, and industry audiences, while modeling AI-native product management across discovery, synthesis, prototyping, roadmap exploration, and concept development.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience leading product managers, including developing senior and principal talent, hiring, and addressing performance directly.</li> <li value="2">A track record of owning a portfolio across multiple product areas and being accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue, not only roadmap delivery.</li> <li value="3">Product management depth in one or more relevant areas, such as continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, artifact or package management, release management, or observability.</li> <li value="4">Sound judgment about where to invest and where to stop, including experience making and defending build, buy, or partner decisions with a business case.</li> <li value="5">Technical fluency to work with engineers along with a thoughtful view of how AI and agentic workflows are changing software delivery. You'll own the outcomes of GitLab's social function — strategy, budget, team development, tooling, and results — and serve as GitLab's senior-most voice on social strategy with executive stakeholders.</p> <p>This is a player-coach role. Two Social Media Managers report to the head of corporate communication and work with you on a dotted-line basis. You'll set their strategic direction, raise the editorial and craft bar, and develop them as practitioners, including goal-setting, feedback, and career development in partnership with their manager. Influence matters in this role, which is why it calls for someone who has already led and grown social practitioners. </p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the performance of GitLab's social function and its contribution to marketing and business goals.</li> <li>Lead GitLab's global organic social media strategy, channel plans, and editorial priorities.</li> <li>Own optimization, and subscriber and watch-time growth.</li> <li>Partner with Growth Marketing on paid social, including briefing creative, aligning organic and paid on shared audiences and messaging, informing boosting and amplification decisions, and connecting paid performance back to organic strategy.</li> <li>Develop clear, audience-focused campaigns that support company, product, brand, and talent goals.</li> <li>Guide content planning and publishing across social channels while maintaining a consistent GitLab voice.</li> <li>Own the social media budget, tooling stack, and agency, freelance, and production partner relationships.</li> <li>Partner with teams across Marketing, Communications, Product, Sales, Talent Acquisition, and other functions to plan and deliver social programs.</li> <li>Build processes that support effective collaboration in GitLab's all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>Use social listening, audience insights, and performance data to improve content and inform broader marketing decisions.</li> <li>Lead the measurement framework for social — KPIs, dashboards, and reporting cadence — and report performance and learnings to marketing and executive leadership.</li> <li>Partner with DevRel on community engagement to help GitLab participate in relevant industry conversations with a clear, useful point of view.</li> <li>Build and run creator, influencer, and advocacy programs, including developer creators, GitLab community contributors, and team member advocacy.</li> <li>Own GitLab's employee advocacy program — grow participation across Marketing, Sales, Engineering, and Talent, equip team members with content worth sharing, and measure reach, engagement, and contribution to brand and talent goals. Partner with Communications and Talent Acquisition on enablement, and manage the advocacy platform and its adoption.</li> <li>Support executive and expert social presence, partnering with Communications to help GitLab leaders and technical experts show up credibly on social, including constructive conversations with C-suite executives about proposed content.</li> <li>Apply AI tools thoughtfully across the social workflow to help GitLab model what an AI-native marketing team looks like.</li> <li>Prepare for and guide responses to sensitive or fast-moving issues in partnership with the appropriate teams.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>10+ years in social media, including at least 5 years leading social strategy for a global brand at the senior manager level or above, and accountable for the function's results.</li> <li>Experience owning a social function end to end, including strategy, budget, headcount, tooling, and results as the accountable leader. </li> <li>Experience leading teams, agencies, and cross-functional programs, with clear ownership of and accountability for outcomes.</li> <li>Depth in YouTube strategy, including owning and growing a brand or business channel, and can speak to programming decisions, video formats, packaging, and the metrics that actually move a channel.</li> <li>Hands-on experience growing LinkedIn and X as primary channels, with judgment about what content, format, and cadence work on each.</li> <li>Experience with paid social programs and how organic and paid social reinforce each other, including creative for paid, audience strategy, and interpreting paid performance data.</li> <li>Experience connecting social media programs to broader brand, communications, product, or business priorities.</li> <li>Strong editorial judgment and the ability to turn complex topics into clear, engaging content.</li> <li>Fluency with short-form and long-form video as core social formats, including working with production partners and creators.</li> <li>Experience defining a measurement framework for social, including KPIs, dashboards, and reporting cadence, and presenting performance, learnings, and recommendations to executive leadership on a standing basis.</li> <li>Experience building or scaling an employee advocacy program, including driving adoption across multiple functions, sustaining participation beyond launch, and reporting attributed reach and business contribution</li> <li>Fluency with an enterprise social stack for publishing, listening, and advocacy. Ours is Sprout Social, Meltwater, and EveryoneSocial.</li> <li>Experience running social programs across multiple regions and languages, and judgment about what to localize versus centralize.</li> <li>Skill in managing multiple priorities and making sound decisions in fast-moving situations.</li> <li>A collaborative, inclusive approach and the ability to work effectively in a distributed, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>Passion about GitLab's mission and the future of software development, open source, artificial intelligence, and DevSecOps.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>This role is part of GitLab's Marketing organization and works across teams to present a clear, consistent company voice on social media. Today, the logic that powers Duo in editors lives inside the GitLab Language Server. We're extracting it into a true software development kit (SDK): a set of well-versioned TypeScript packages that editor extensions, our web-based Duo Chat on GitLab.com, and eventually external applications can use.</p> <p>You'll work in TypeScript across frontend and backend systems. You'll design the SDK's Node.js core and public application programming interface (API), and work in the clients that use it. The work rewards care about interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility as much as features because other engineers will depend on what you build.</p> <p>You'll have senior and staff engineers alongside you to help with design. You'll own the implementation of scoped packages and ship improvements with minimal guidance while collaborating with the team on larger architectural changes.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li>The Duo Client SDK, extracting versioned, publishable packages from the GitLab Language Server</li> <li>The GitLab Language Server, rebuilt on top of the SDK as our polyglot surface</li> <li>Duo Chat on the web, as one of the SDK's first consumers</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Develop secure, well-tested, and performant TypeScript features that solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity.</li> <li>Ship small features and improvements with minimal guidance, writing tests with every merge request and contributing to code reviews and design discussions.</li> <li>Extract and publish TypeScript packages from the GitLab Language Server, migrating consumers incrementally so no parallel implementation is left to drift.</li> <li>Design durable public APIs with clear interfaces, semantic versioning, changelogs, and deprecation paths for external consumers.</li> <li>Build isomorphic core packages that isolate platform-specific behavior in adapters at the edges.</li> <li>Build and improve SDK client surfaces, including Vue 3 components in Duo Chat on the web, in collaboration with product, design, and engineering teams.</li> <li>Strengthen credential handling across hosts, including bearer tokens, session cookies, and CSRF protection.</li> <li>Optimize bundle size, startup cost, and dependency weight for browser consumers, and support a Tier 2 on-call rotation for urgent engineering issues.</li> <li>Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Strong proficiency with TypeScript across frontend and backend systems, including experience building and maintaining Node.js services.</li> <li>Experience with modern build and packaging tools, including monorepos, multi-module builds, ECMAScript modules (ESM), and dependency management.</li> <li>Experience with Vue 3 and the Composition API, or comparable component-based frontend experience and a willingness to learn Vue.</li> <li>Experience designing APIs that other people use, with the ability to explain what you'd do differently.</li> <li>Understanding of the differences between running code in Node.js and in the browser, and how to write code that works in both.</li> <li>A security-minded development approach, including careful credential handling and performance optimization.</li> <li>Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in writing about technical problems, propose iterative solutions, and work effectively in an agile environment.</li> <li>Self-motivation, strong organizational skills, and the judgment to ask for help when needed while thriving in a fully remote organization aligned with GitLab's values.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Duo Client SDK team sits in GitLab's AI Clients stage and works closely with teams building GitLab Duo experiences. We collaborate across client surfaces to make thoughtful technical decisions as the platform evolves. We work fully remotely and asynchronously across regions, in the open, following GitLab's values of transparency and open communication.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: title: Intermediate Fullstack Engineer, Subscription Lifecycle
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As an Intermediate Fullstack Engineer on GitLab's Subscription Lifecycle team within Monetization, you'll build the frontend experiences and backend services customers use to view and manage subscriptions, renew products, configure auto-renewal, and manage billing accounts. (preferred) or React.</li> <li value="2">Experience owning technical direction for a product area, including proposing, discussing, and driving thorough, iterative solutions.</li> <li value="3">Experience building or maintaining transactional or checkout-style flows, ideally in a billing, ecommerce, or subscription context.</li> <li value="4">Familiarity integrating with third-party billing or customer relationship management systems, such as Zuora, Salesforce, or Stripe, is a plus, not a requirement.</li> <li value="5">A focus on safe, incremental delivery given the revenue and customer impact of this work.</li> <li value="6">The ability to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems and propose thorough, iterative solutions.</li> <li value="7">Written and spoken English proficiency sufficient to collaborate in a remote, largely asynchronous work environment.</li> <li value="8">Alignment with GitLab's values and a commitment to working in accordance with them.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Subscription Lifecycle team is part of GitLab's Monetization section and owns the post-purchase subscription experience. You'll partner with Sales, Finance, Information Technology, and Support on secure, reliable purchasing, billing, provisioning, and utilization workflows, and report to the Engineering Manager, Purchase. The team works asynchronously, with regular planning and retrospectives and shared expectations for deployments, incident management, testing, and rollout safety. GitLab's mission is to enable everyone to contribute and co-create the software that powers our world. The Purchase team's mission is to make it as easy as possible for anyone to buy, add on to, or upgrade GitLab through a single, trustworthy, unified purchase experience. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. You will identify and activate advocates and their stories that showcase customer outcomes, support pipeline and revenue goals, and deepen trust in GitLab across Asia Pacific and Japan.</p> <p>Reporting into the growth marketing organization, you will own the day-to-day development and delivery of customer advocacy initiatives in close partnership with APJ sales, marketing, and global teams. You will build trusted customer relationships, identify stories and advocates, and connect the right customers to references, campaigns, events, and executive engagements. Because APJ spans diverse markets, cultures, and time zones, you will tailor engagement to local context while creating programs that scale and align with global priorities.</p> <p>In your first year, you will establish clear, measurable advocacy goals for the region, strengthen collaboration with regional stakeholders, and increase the visibility of customer outcomes across go-to-market motions. This is an opportunity to bring the voice of APJ customers forward and demonstrate GitLab’s impact on their business.</p> <h2><strong>Some Examples of Our Projects</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Partnering with sales, pre-sales, and marketing to turn complex customer solutions into compelling narratives for campaigns, events, and executive engagements</li> <li>Creating and executing customer references, case studies, speaking opportunities, and other advocacy activities and programs across APJ markets</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What You’ll Do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the APJ customer story, reference and proof library, and associated pipeline.</li> <li>Build and nurture relationships with customer advocates, including senior stakeholders, and identify opportunities for references, case studies, events, and thought leadership.</li> <li>Manage the customer advocacy lifecycle: identify and recruit advocates, understand their goals, coordinate participation, and maintain mutually valuable relationships over time.</li> <li>Bring the voice of the customer into GitLab’s narratives, campaigns, and go-to-market plans by working with internal stakeholders to develop and amplify customer stories.</li> <li>Partner with regional and global sales, marketing, customer success, and product teams to align advocacy initiatives with pipeline, expansion, and retention priorities.</li> Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As SEC Manager on GitLab’s Accounting team, you’ll take end-to-end ownership of our external financial reporting, including Forms 10-K and 10-Q. This isn’t a collect-and-consolidate role. You’ll drive the reporting calendar, coordinate work across Accounting, Legal, Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), and Investor Relations, and improve the quality, clarity, and consistency of our disclosures and reporting processes. You’ll report to the Director of SEC Reporting and work remotely from the Americas.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the preparation, review, and filing of GitLab’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filings, including Forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K, and S-1, along with quarterly investor materials.</li> <li>Build and drive the quarterly and annual reporting calendar, coordinate cross-functional inputs, maintain accountability for deadlines, and flag timeline risks early.</li> <li>Lead the earnings release process, including the quarterly management reporting package and review of financial information in the earnings release and script.</li> <li>Own the disclosure checklist and eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) review process, and identify ways to improve disclosure quality, clarity, and consistency.</li> <li>Improve the SEC reporting process by identifying inefficiencies, redundancies, and manual steps, then driving automation and standardization.</li> <li>Prepare or review journal entries, reconciliations, the equity rollforward, earnings per share calculations, and provided-by-client schedules for assigned areas such as stock-based compensation and stock repurchases.</li> <li>Ensure compliance with SEC and United States generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP) reporting requirements, research technical accounting issues, and lead the implementation of new accounting pronouncements that affect disclosures.</li> <li>Maintain Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) requirements for relevant areas, support internal and external reporting packages, and lead or contribute to special projects such as process improvements, new disclosure requirements, and merger and acquisition reporting.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>A bachelor’s degree in Accounting.</li> <li>Certified Public Accountant (CPA) licensure or active pursuit of licensure is preferred.</li> <li>Experience in owning SEC reporting deliverables, including Forms 10-K and 10-Q, in a public company or a public accounting environment serving public company clients.</li> <li>A record of improving disclosures and reporting processes, not only executing existing processes.</li> <li>Strong project management skills, with the ability to own a calendar, drive accountability across teams, and manage competing deadlines independently.</li> <li>Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to research and interpret complex accounting guidance.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal You stay calm, keep people aligned, and know when to bring in leadership.</li> <li>The ability to turn a complicated or nuanced situation into a clear written story and tie activity to outcomes with numbers.</li> <li>A customer-centric approach balanced with good judgment about what the service, the team, and the company can deliver, and experience working with account teams to bring struggling customers back to health.</li> <li>A record of getting work done across teams through influence and strong working relationships.
